absent: Numeric values and bit layouts of capability identifiers, masks, MSR numbers, CPUID leaves and feature bits
Internals of TSC helpers, time scaling, Hyper-V TSC page update and Xen runstate update
Sequence counter and raw spinlock semantics and cross-subsystem lock ordering
Guest mapping cache refresh, dirty tracking and memslot generation lifecycle
Full error mapping and userspace structure layouts for CPUID, MSR, LAPIC and device attribute ioctls
Vendor-specific TLB flush, APIC state and nested state helpers

findings.text: Refresh routine for one VCPU clock is externally callable, reports normal completion versus deferred retry, and fans out to guest, Hyper-V and Xen time pages when active.
Extension query routine is externally callable and maps a capability identifier plus optional VM context to an integer capability answer.
Device control routine for the x86 KVM device is externally callable and dispatches MSR, CPUID, Hyper-V CPUID, MCE cap and device attribute operations.

VM master clock is enabled only when host time derives from TSC, all online VCPUs match TSC, no backwards TSC was seen, and boot VCPU does not use old kvmclock; enabling sets a global guest master clock indicator and emits a trace of the decision inputs.
Shared time copy is protected by a TSC write lock held across mutation plus a sequence counter bracketing the update; readers sample the counter around the master cycle and kernel time values.

Master refresh moves from broadcast of an in-progress request to all CPUs, to locked sequence begin that blocks guest entry, to shared copy update, to sequence end and unlock, then per-VCPU clock update requests and clearing of the in-progress marker to reallow entry.

Guest clock publication stages a reference image, validates the mapping with refresh retry, publishes with odd version during mutation and even version when consistent, preserves a stopped flag found in the guest, marks the slot dirty and traces the VCPU result.
Guest clock mapping is accessed under a reader lock with interrupts saved; on validation failure the lock is dropped for refresh and reacquired before rechecking.

Per-VCPU time calculation prefers the shared master cycle and kernel time when the master flag is set, otherwise samples current TSC and base time under disabled interrupts, applies catch-up adjustment and optional TSC scaling, and caches shift and multiplier only when the target rate changes.

Published flags mark TSC stable only when the master clock is in use, optionally set a guest-stopped indication once per request for active pv time, clear that indication for the Hyper-V page, and for Xen may clear stable when configured unstable before writing Xen info caches at their defined offsets.
A zero host TSC rate aborts the update, restores interrupts, re-requests a clock update for the VCPU and signals the caller to retry later.
Global kvmclock refresh requests a clock update on every VCPU of the VM and kicks each VCPU out of guest state.
Full TLB flush for a VCPU increments that VCPU flush counter, invokes the vendor flush operation, and clears any pending flush-current request because all address spaces were flushed.

Steal accounting is skipped for Xen runstate guests by marking running, skipped when the steal MSR is disabled, aborted on address space mismatch, and otherwise validates generation, address, error handle and slot before initializing the host mapping sized to one page.

Steal record update handles a paravirtual TLB flush feature by atomically exchanging the preempted byte and conditionally flushing guest TLB, otherwise clears preempted, then advances version from odd to even around accumulation of scheduling delay into the steal counter.
Steal path treats user access begin failures, faulting user accesses and invalid host mappings as silent aborts, yet still marks the backing slot page dirty on paths that reached user mapping.

MWAIT may stay in the guest only with MWAIT and always-running timer support and without a monitor bug; the allowed exit-disable mask always permits pause, adds aperf/mperf when present, and adds halt, cstate and possibly mwait only when a microcode mitigation is off.
VM type support requires an index below thirty-two present in a supported bitmask; synchronized register fields are empty for protected-state VMs and a fixed valid set otherwise.

A large family of capability queries covering interrupt, timer, identity, debug, PMU filter, guest mode and related features carries an affirmative value, with Hyper-V, PIT and SGX members present only under the corresponding builds.

Dynamic capability answers include TDP-gated pre-fault, per-VM APIC bus timing, hypercall exit mask, guest debug mask, Xen feature combination with optional runstate bits, sync register set, clock flags, exit-disable mask, SMM probe, CPU count bounds, MCE bank count, XSAVE presence, TSC control, X2APIC flags with split-irqchip conditioning, nested state size, direct TLB flush and enlightened VMCS presence, smaller address width, steal availability, bus lock detection, XSAVE2 size, PMU mask, quirk mask, notify mask, VM type mask and readonly memory support.
Supported Hyper-V CPUID query copies a header from userspace, fills entries through a helper, copies the header back, and propagates fault or helper failure codes.

Device attribute access routes nonzero groups to a vendor hook and otherwise serves a guest XCR0 support value; get copies out to userspace while has only probes success, both reporting missing attribute or fault appropriately.

Arch device control dispatches MSR list, supported and emulated CPUID, MCE capability, feature MSR list and values, Hyper-V CPUID when built, and device attribute get and probe operations, rejecting unknown commands.

Guest clock record carries a version sequence, flags, TSC shift and scale multiplier, TSC timestamp and system time; system time adds VM kvmclock offset to sampled kernel time and the VCPU caches the last guest TSC.

Steal record carries a version sequence, a preempted indicator and an accumulated steal counter; the host also caches mapping generation, address, slot, last scheduling delay and a software preempted flag per VCPU.
A per-CPU pointer caches the last VCPU that ran on that CPU.
LAPIC state get and set are rejected when the guest APIC is protected; get synchronizes posted interrupts before reading state while set writes state and propagates its status.
Xen running-state helper unconditionally transitions the target VCPU to the running runstate.
